subject: Round 1–2: AegisCloud DPA redlines, transfer evidence & eSign path
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aegiscloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Round 1–2: AegisCloud DPA redlines, transfer evidence & eSign path
Attachments: Aegis_DPA_Redline_v1.pdf (redline stub)

Hi Samir —

Thanks for sending the candidate DPA. Attached is our initial redline (round 1) with a few flag items we want to call out up front so you and Elena can review before our next call: 

- Transfers & SCCs: we’ve proposed the EU–US Addendum approach you suggested but added language allowing Redwood to rely on SCCs or the EU–UK Addendum depending on regs in scope. We left an explicit fallback that requires written notice before using an alternate mechanism.
- Subprocessors: we accepted a process for 30-day notice for new subprocessor additions but limited the carve-out for essential infra partners that are separately audited (SOC 2). See section 3.2 comments.
- Evidence: Aegis asked for "logs showing process access for 3 months" — we provided an evidence inventory template (CSV) and noted which items we can provide by export (audit logs, account admin change history) vs. which require a custom report/pull (KV cache access, ephemeral GPU logs).
- Escrow/logging: you mentioned "escrow logs" on the call; that typically maps to immutable audit exports. We can produce periodic signed exports under an SOW.
- eSign & signatories: propose DocuSign route; Redwood requires Company officer + delegated contract signatory (name placeholder ok for now).

Marissa, I’m looping you for counsel’s annotated notes — any items that should be escalated or rephrased?

Next steps: if Aegis is comfortable we’ll take these redlines into round 2 and prepare an execution packet (DocuSign envelope + evidence bundle). Please confirm availability for a 30-min sync Thursday.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@aegiscloud.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Round 1–2: AegisCloud DPA redlines, transfer evidence & eSign path
Attachments: Redwood_Privacy_Counsel_Notes_20280415.docx (annotated)

Irene / Samir — forwarding our annotated counsel notes. I kept comments inline in the redline where possible; key counsel recommendations summarized below (high-level):

1) Transfers: Counsel prefers an explicit reference to the exact SCC version we will rely on and a mechanism to update the transfer basis without substantive amendments (notification + 30 days). Avoids re-signing large customers for administrative updates.

2) Subprocessors & carve-outs: Counsel asked to add a short control objective for "critical infra subprocessors" (those with persistent access to plaintext or long-term storage) so we can justify a 14-day notice exception where needed for security operations. They recommend enumerating examples (e.g., cloud provider backup service, managed database operator) rather than broad categories.

3) Evidence scope: Counsel flagged requests for "GPU ephemeral logs" as operationally heavy and suggested we respond with a scope-limited alternative (summaries + signed attestations) and offer an SOW for custom forensic exports.

4) Liability caps / residuals: redline tightens language around mutual indemnities related to subprocessors; counsel recommends a 24-month lookback for indicated events and an explicit exclusion for pre-existing vulnerabilities.

5) Execution & retention: counsel wants to ensure the eSign flow includes an executed Annex record (timestamped) and retention metadata in DocuSign for audit. I attached a sample envelope preview.

Samir, happy to set up a short call so counsel and your legal team can align on transfer basis and the evidence matrix. If we can agree on the evidence inventory template, we can attach it to the DocuSign packet to avoid back-and-forth.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Irene / Marissa — thanks for the fast turnaround and the detailed counsel notes. A couple quick items from Aegis legal priorities: 

- Transfer basis: we prefer the SCC route too; can you confirm Redwood's standard SCC attachment (version and date) and whether Redwood will act as data importer for the purposes of the Addendum?
- Escrow & logs: Aegis needs a signed, time-stamped export that shows administrative access events for the prior 90 days (who, when, what). We understand GPU ephemeral logs may be heavy — the CSV you provided helps. Can Redwood commit to a monthly scheduled export or is on-demand only?
- Subprocessor carve-outs: Aegis is open to a short list approach but wants the list published and updated on the portal with 14-day notice. Is a portal notice + email confirmation okay?
- Liability: we'll push back on a 24-month lookback for all events; can we agree to event-specific windows (e.g., 12 months for admin access, 36 months for data exfiltration incidents)?

If that covers most items, Elena and I can propose narrow countertext for transfer/notice clauses and share in advance of the call. We are free Thursday 4/19 10:00–11:00 PT.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Infrastructure Security, AegisCloud

Samir — great, Thursday 4/19 10:00 PT works for us. Quick responses inline to your asks: 

- SCC attachment: Redwood will use the EU SCCs (2021 standard) and we can include the specific attachment in the execution packet. We do act as data importer where Redwood is processing on behalf of the customer (we'll add clarifying language).
- Export cadence: we can commit to a scheduled monthly signed export for administrative access events for the last 90 days; on-demand forensic exports are available under an SOW (standard hourly rates apply). The monthly export will be in CSV with a signed custody hash.
- Subprocessor notices: portal posting + email confirmation is acceptable. We'll add commit to publish the current subprocessor list on our public portal and send a certifying email to the primary contact.

Marissa — per counsel's note, can you draft the short carve-out definition for "critical infra subprocessors" with two concrete examples? That will speed Elena's review.

Aditya — I asked ops to generate the first sample export for the call; can you confirm ETA and attach the sample to the DocuSign packet so Elena can preview?

Samir / Elena — I’ll generate the DocuSign envelope with the redline + counsel notes + evidence inventory attached and send the preview link ahead of Thursday. Looking forward to aligning.

Irene
